title: Make release metadata parsing syntax-aware and diagnostics deterministic
problem: Verified: tools/check-release.py parses TOML with regexes, checks changelog headings by substring, and exposes missing or unreadable release files as tracebacks. Proposed: use syntax-aware parsing, exact heading validation, and actionable fail-closed errors.
acceptance: Proposed acceptance: reordered keys, comments, supported quoted forms, malformed TOML, and missing or unreadable required files are covered on supported Python versions; invalid inputs return nonzero actionable diagnostics without tracebacks.
Proposed acceptance: only a line-anchored `## [X.Y.Z]` changelog heading, allowing the existing date suffix, passes; prose, fenced text, and near matches fail.
Proposed acceptance: `python tools/check-release.py` and `python -m pytest -q tests/test_release.py` pass.

title: Verify both built artifacts before PyPI publication
problem: Verified: .github/workflows/release.yml builds a wheel and source distribution but only installs and smoke-tests the wheel; the publish job downloads the artifacts without an independent artifact-set or digest check. Existing packaging tests inspect the sdist and install the wheel, but do not install-test the sdist. Proposed: bind publication to a fully validated wheel and sdist.
acceptance: Proposed acceptance: release validation rejects missing, duplicate, unexpected, or version-mismatched wheel and sdist files before upload.

Proposed acceptance: clean environments outside the checkout install both artifacts and run `pi-batch --version`, `pi-batch version --json`, `pi-batch tui --help`, and a packaged-validator smoke test.
Proposed acceptance: a manifest or digest produced during verification is checked before publication; replacing either artifact causes publication to fail.
Proposed acceptance: `python -m pytest -q tests/test_release.py tests/test_packaging.py` passes with explicit sdist installation coverage.
